newsitem.title: TURKEY: Siemens-Ansaldo win Turkish light rail tender.
newsitem.headline: Siemens-Ansaldo win Turkish light rail tender.

text.p: A consortium led by German Siemens and Italy's Ansaldo won a tender to build a light rail system in the western Turkish city of Bursa for 459 million marks plus $35 million, the semi-official Anatolian news agency said on Friday.
It said the consortium also included Siemens' Turkish subsidiary Simko, Turkish construction firm Guris and state train carriage maker Tuvasas.
The agency said the 20.6-km line would be completed in 700 days and would include underground tunnels.
The contract will be signed by January 24 between Bursa city council and the winning consortium, the agency quoted Bursa mayor Erdem Saker as saying.
A total of 24 bids were received for the tender which closed in April 1996. The short list included two other consortia -- Adtranz - Turkish Yapi Merkezi and GEC Alsthom-Turkish STFA.
The agency also said the German government would provide the city with a 147-million-mark, 30-year soft loan including 10-year grace period for the project.
"Work will begin immediately after the Turkish Treasury approves the light rail contract," Saker was quoted as saying.
Tuvasas would construct 48 carriages for the light rail system which will be extended to a total of 48 km in the future.
